verdicts.evidence: The ST−OR bias table from n=4000, 8-rep synthetic runs shows IBS bias varying sharply by mechanism at 80% censoring (administrative −0.0795, independent −0.0323, covariate-dependent 0.0000) and increasing monotonically with censoring rate, while C-index bias grows with rate (+0.0022→+0.0270 for admin) — directly demonstrating systematic, rate- and mechanism-dependent distortions.

Ranking-agreement tables from 24-rep runs show near-tied model rankings matching the oracle only 29–42% of the time at 80% censoring (down from 100% at 0%), while widely-separated models retain 100% agreement — confirming that moderate metric bias (~0.03 C-index shift) destabilizes model comparison specifically in the near-tied regime as censoring increases.

overall: The logbook executes a faithful ST-vs-OR experimental design with concrete numerical results that directly support both claims: mechanism-dependent metric distortions (especially in IBS) and ranking instability under heavy censoring for near-tied models. The purely synthetic DGP is a methodologically appropriate choice for isolating censoring effects with known ground truth, though it is a scope reduction from the paper's semi-synthetic real-dataset experiments.
